title: A flow mapping of thirty thousand pairs on one line
notes: The input is valid: the keys are the numbers 0 to 29999, all different. An implicit key is at most 1024 characters on one line, so a pending key candidate expires once it is that far behind, and time and memory must stay linear in the length of the line. A reader that keeps every candidate of a long line pending used 931 MB for a ten megabyte line; at the size stored here it stays under the bound, so the case pins the exact events of a long one-line mapping and the bounds are only a guard. The bounds are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. Input: `{`, then `0: v, `, `1: v, ` and so on up to `29999: v, `, then `}`.

provenance.reference: A reader that kept every possible implicit key of a long one-line flow mapping in a queue, using 931 MB for a ten megabyte line.
